thread:
maria: Heads-up — I'm prototyping async/batched authz at the edge to reduce per-token rps. Question: if we collapse N incoming requests into one authz evaluation, how should we handle quota/billing attribution and audit logs? Want to avoid hiding owner identity when we write usage metrics.

alex: High level: we need 1) accurate billing attribution, 2) clear audit trail, 3) low overhead on edge. My thought: keep per-subrequest metadata and send a compact batch payload to auth service that includes origin markers for each subrequest. The auth service returns a list of decisions keyed by subrequest id. That way quotas are applied per origin. But payload size + serialization is a concern.

sam: Two gotchas: cache staleness (decisions change) and quota double-counting when multiple edges retry. Also billing pipelines expect one event per token/request. If we batch, we either emit N events (preferred) or emit 1 aggregated event and lose granularity. Which do we want? :thinking: 
maria: Ideally we emit N events downstream, but don't want the edge to do N separate network writes. Maybe edge writes a single compressed envelope to telemetry and downstream decomposes it into N events asynchronously. Thoughts?
alex: That could work. Pattern: edge assigns per-subrequest decision_id and attribution tuple {org, project, service_account, request_id}. Send batch to auth service, get back decisions + decision_ids. Edge emits a single telemetry envelope with items: [ {decision_id, attribution, cost_tokens, outcome}... ] — telemetry pipeline expands it. This preserves granularity while keeping edge I/O small.
sam: Also need a stable trace id to link envelope -> expanded events for console drilldown. Add decision_id and trace_id to audit log entries so admin can drill into the N items.
maria: UX question: console shows per-route token breakdown today. If we batch, some devs will see aggregated numbers that don't match per-request logs. Proposal: show aggregated by default but surface a "Show batch details" drilldown which pulls decomposed events (or the original envelope) by trace_id.
alex: Implementation notes: add headers for attribution and trace. Example header we can standardize on: 
```
X-RW-Attribution: org=org_123;project=proj_456;sa=svc-a;token_hash=sha256:abc...
X-RW-Trace: trace=trace-20231101-xxxxx
X-RW-Decision-IDs: d1,d2,d3
```
Edge attaches one header per envelope, body contains per-item compact records. Auth service returns decisions in same order.
auth-bot: (automated) Reminder: audit retention and PII policy — storing token_hash is allowed but raw tokens MUST NOT be logged. See https://redwood.internal/policy/logging for details.
sam: For quotas: auth service should run attribution logic and emit quota usage events per item to billing. That prevents counting the envelope as one unit. Need idempotency keys so retries don't double-burn quotas. Suggest include per-item idempotency key derived from (token_hash, request_id, timestamp_bucket).
maria: Good point on idempotency. For rollout: do a canary where only 5% of traffic uses batching and we mirror quota events to validate parity. Also flag to fall back to per-request authz on mismatch.
alex: I'll sketch the proposal + perf numbers. Will add schema for envelope and telemetry expansion step.
sam: I'll write a short runbook for oncall: how to detect if batching causes under/over billing and how to revert.
maria: Thanks — please put PR in draft and ping #eng-platform when ready. (reacted with :thumbsup:)
